S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder involves the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor, occurring within months of the event and causing marked distress or functional impairment beyond what would be expected. Clinically, it often presents with mood changes, anxiety, or maladaptive behaviors tied closely in time and content to specific life events such as relationship conflict, health changes, or occupational stress. The course is typically time-limited, with symptoms resolving within six months after the stressor or its consequences end, though it can persist if the stressor is ongoing. It is distinguished from normal stress reactions by the degree of impairment and from other disorders (e.g., major depression, PTSD) by its less severe, more situationally bound presentation and the absence of defining features such as full depressive episodes or trauma-related re-experiencing.

patient.stressor: Five months ago, Maria’s school district implemented a sudden restructuring that reassigned her from her long-standing bilingual classroom to a larger, mixed-ability class with a rigid scripted curriculum, while also cutting the arts-integrated and social-emotional programs she had helped build. At the same time, new evaluation metrics tied to standardized test scores placed intense pressure on veteran teachers like her, and several close colleagues either retired early or transferred, leaving her feeling isolated and undermined in the work that had anchored her identity for decades. Over the following months, she brought more grading and planning home, stopped enjoying her watercolor sessions and salsa nights, and began dreading each school day, noticing that her usual optimism and mentoring energy had been replaced by a sense that she was constantly failing her students under the new system. After her principal gently noted a decline in her classroom engagement and she caught herself snapping at a student for a minor behavior issue—something very out of character—she agreed to her sister’s suggestion to seek psychiatric help because she felt her reactions to the changes at work were overwhelming her and spilling into every part of her life.
patient.chief_complaint: Ever since they changed everything at school, I feel like I’m not handling it well at all and my reactions to the stress are taking over my life.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: Ever since they upended everything at school, I feel like I’m on this constant emotional roller coaster—crying in my car before work, snapping at kids and my husband over tiny things, lying awake replaying test scores and new scripts in my head—and it scares me how unlike myself I’ve become and how much it’s seeping into every corner of my life.

add_requirements.within_3_months_of_stressor: Within a few weeks of them announcing the restructuring and moving me into the new class, I went from feeling like my usual, grounded self to crying in the parking lot before school and dreading walking into my classroom.
add_requirements.within_6_months_of_termination: I keep telling myself that if they ever ease up on these new test-score demands or let me go back to the kind of teaching I used to do, I could see myself finally calming down instead of living in this constant state of work-related tension.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: My lesson planning has slowed to the point where I’m staying up late every night just to keep up, my principal has commented that I seem disengaged in class, and at home I’m so drained and irritable that I’ve been skipping family get‑togethers and barely talking to my husband in the evenings.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about five months now, basically since they rolled out all the changes at my school.
